=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/stage_switch_watch.sh:148-180 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: If jq fails to parse the evaluation counts, `alert_count` falls back to 0, so the alert loop is skipped and every alert in `result` is silently dropped for that run.
  WHY: The `counts:-0 0 0 0` fallback means `for ((idx = 0; idx < alert_count; idx++))` / `if [ "${alert_count:-0}" != "0" ]` never runs even though `result` already holds the evaluated alerts; the run logs `alerts=0 alert=none`, writes no day marker, and the alerts only return on the next day's run. Both reviewers rated it MAJOR. anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 and z-ai_glm-5_3-flash did not report it: they consider the path unreachable or an accepted, documented trade-off.
- scripts/stage_switch_watch.sh:197-199 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: When `mkdir -p` succeeds but the `date -u +%F > day.txt` write fails, the `&& ... || true` chain still succeeds, so `alerted=true` is emitted with no marker actually written.
  WHY: A later run the same day hits the cache and logs `alert=already_sent_today`, which silences every later alert that day without a real marker ever having been saved (source severity NIT).
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: "The list of switches and defaults comes from one source that a test keeps in step with the workflows' `vars.<NAME> || '<default>'` expressions, so a new switch cannot be added without being covered."
  expected_change_site: tests/test_stage_switch_registry.py, `_workflow_true_switches`
  confidence=4
  flagged_by: [openai_gpt-6-luna]
  EVIDENCE: Lines 60–68 split each workflow into lines and run the expression regex on each line separately, so a multiline expression with the switch name on one line and `|| 'true'` on another is not detected. If that switch is also missing from the README tables, the test does not require it in the registry and the watch will not report it (source severity NIT).
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
(No findings reported.)
- HARDENING: scripts/stage_switch_watch.sh | stage_switch_report, send loop, `msg_id="$(tg_send_msg "${msg}" WARNING 2>/dev/null)" || msg_id=""`
  PROBLEM: `2>/dev/null` discards the failure reason tg_send_msg writes to stderr (scripts/tg_helpers.sh lines 151 and 158), so an `alert=not_delivered` run, including partial delivery, gives no cause; the stderr text is already sanitized (line 157).
  WHY: A rate limit cannot be told apart from a wrong chat id. Fix: remove `2>/dev/null` (1 line). HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1
- HARDENING: scripts/stage_switch_watch.sh | stage_switch_report, warning after counts jq extraction (`could not parse the evaluation counts; the counts below read 0.`)
  PROBLEM: When this path fires, alert_count is 0, so alerts are skipped and no day marker is written, but the warning does not say so.
  WHY: Fix: add "alerts are skipped this run" to the warning (1 line). The reviewer considers the jq-failure path unrealistic: GitHub-hosted Ubuntu ships jq, and tg_send_msg needs jq too. HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1
=== END FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- scripts/stage_switch_watch.sh:lines 148-152 (parsing counts) and 172-180 (alert loop) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The alert loop is silently skipped if jq fails to parse the evaluation counts.
  WHY: An empty counts value falls back to `counts:-0 0 0 0`, so alert_count=0 and the loop does not run even though `result` holds alerts, which silently suppresses all alerts for that run.
- HARDENING: scripts/stage_switch_watch.sh | line 176 (tg_send_msg call)
  PROBLEM: `2>/dev/null` suppresses tg_send_msg diagnostic output on failure.
  WHY: This makes send failures hard to debug. Fix: remove `2>/dev/null` (1 line). HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/stage_switch_watch.sh:lines 148-153 (counts extraction) and line 172 (`if [ "${alert_count:-0}" != "0" ]`) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The new "counts parse failed" warning at line 150 makes the jq failure visible, but the alert loop is still skipped because `alert_count` falls back to 0.
  WHY: With jq missing or failing, every alert is dropped: the run logs `outcome=ok ... alerts=0 alert=none` and writes no day marker. `result` is already in scope, so the counts could be read without jq (e.g. a python3 one-liner).
- scripts/stage_switch_watch.sh:lines 197-199, the `mkdir -p "${stage_switch_alert_marker_dir}" 2>/dev/null && date -u +%F > "${stage_switch_alert_marker_dir}/day.txt" 2>/dev/null || true` line | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: A failed day.txt write still collapses to success, so `alerted=true` fires and the cache step runs on an empty or missing marker directory.
  WHY: A later run the same day logs `alert=already_sent_today`, which silences that day's alerts without a real marker.
- HARDENING: scripts/stage_switch_watch.sh | send loop, `msg_id="$(tg_send_msg "${msg}" WARNING 2>/dev/null)"`
  PROBLEM: `2>/dev/null` discards the tg_helpers.sh stderr diagnostics, so `alert=not_delivered` runs (including partial delivery) give no clue why.
  WHY: Fix: drop `2>/dev/null`; redaction already happens inside tg_helpers.sh (1 line). HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1
- HARDENING: scripts/stage_switch_watch.sh | stage_switch_report, lines 148-153 (jq counts extraction)
  PROBLEM: jq is a hard dependency for the counts even though `result` is a JSON string already in scope.
  WHY: Fix: replace the jq subshell with a python3 one-liner reading `['counts']` (2 lines). HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 3
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
